reason: The cited evidence supports that 500°C treatment gives highest microhardness and lowest wear rate, and that 700°C treatment reduces hardness and increases wear, but it does not mention oxide layer formation, solid lubrication, or spallation mechanisms, leaving several key premises unsupported.
premises: Thermal pre-treatment at ~500°C yields highest microhardness and best wear resistance in FeNiCrCoCu coatings
Thermal pre-treatment at ~700°C reduces microhardness and increases wear rate
A protective, adherent oxide layer forms during thermal exposure and governs wear resistance
The oxide layer acts as a solid lubricant, reducing friction
Excessive thermal exposure causes oxide spallation and grain coarsening that degrade wear resistance
